issues.description: Template constructor declares the query register as self._query_register but then uses self.query_register when constructing the QuantumCircuit (and elsewhere). This inconsistent attribute naming (self._query_register vs self.query_register) will cause AttributeError/NameError when students run or extend the template and prevents them from following the intended initialization pattern shown in the solution, which consistently uses self.query_register. This is a structural bug in the template (not an intentional pedagogical omission) and will block students trying to run or complete Exercise 1.1 and subsequent methods that rely on self.query_register.
issues.suggested_fix:
Make the attribute name consistent in the template constructor. Replace self._query_register with self.query_register (or use self._query_register everywhere consistently). For example:
- set self.query_register = QuantumRegister(self.number_of_qubits_query_register)
- then create the circuit with self.qc = QuantumCircuit(self.query_register)
This aligns the template with the problem description and the solution, removing the runtime/name-error barrier for students.

This inconsistent attribute name breaks the conceptual mapping between the problem description's 'query register' and the template implementation, and will cause runtime errors (AttributeError) or confusion for students trying to use the provided query_register in later methods and the run() helper.
issues.suggested_fix: In the template (template_repository/ex1_grover_two_qubit_without_auxiliary_qubit.py) make the attribute name consistent with the rest of the code and the solution. Replace self._query_register = QuantumRegister(...) with self.query_register = QuantumRegister(...), or else update all later references to use self._query_register. Preferred: use self.query_register to match the method signatures and the solution implementation.
